title: Build the inequality from a word model
subtitle: Linear inequalities in one or two variables · 20 official questions

sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **20 of the official questions in Linear inequalities in one or two variables are this one** — 9 Easy, 7 Medium, 4 Hard.
It is bottom-heavy, which makes it cheap points. Secure it early.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:
- A longer stem describes costs, earnings, dimensions, ticket sales or a chain of numbers, plus a limit ('budget', 'cannot exceed', 'at least … times', 'is at most … less than').
- All four choices are inequalities that look almost the same.
- They differ in the direction of the sign, the order of subtraction, or one coefficient.

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) Write the expression for the quantity in variables, e.g. rate × count + fixed fee, or perimeter + height.
- Name any hidden terms, such as the next consecutive odd integer = n + 2.
- 2) Translate the limit word into a sign: 'at most', 'no more than', 'cannot exceed' and 'budget' mean ≤; 'at least' and 'minimum' mean ≥.
- 3) Put the pieces in the order the words give them. 'k less than X' is X − k, not k − X.
- Then match to a choice, simplifying first if the choices are simplified.

sections.heading: Where Desmos fits
body: Only useful as a check.
Type your inequality and each choice, then compare the shaded regions or solution intervals.
If two are identical, they are equivalent forms.
Desmos cannot do the translation for you.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: You write 'k less than X' as k − X, use the wrong sign for 'at most' or 'minimum', or use n + 1 instead of n + 2 for consecutive odd integers.
Wrong choices are built from exactly these swaps, including one that fits 'maximum' when the stem says 'minimum'.

sections.heading: You are losing these
